policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 9 Jan close (1x4 3.79, 3x6 3.58, 6x9 3.43, 9x12 3.39 vs WIBOR 3M 3.95) price roughly 55bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026. PKO (7 Jan): derivatives price a 3.25% reference rate by mid-2026; Deutsche Bank Polska (7 Jan) expects a January hold with core CPI at ~2.8%. MPC member Dąbrowski (Bloomberg, 8 Jan): a 50% chance of a January cut after the low December CPI, though he leans to a pause, and room for another 50bp by mid-2026; Tyrowicz (8 Jan): CPI may stay near target for the first time in this episode.
policy.risk_text: The January decision is a coin-toss for some members (Dąbrowski, 8 Jan) while most economists expect a hold: a hold would lift short FRAs/IRS a few bp (Millennium, 12-13 Jan), a cut would extend the front-end rally (PKO). If cuts are pushed beyond March, front-end roll-down does not materialise; heavy Q1 supply can widen asset swaps (Millennium, 9 Jan).

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~6.9% of GDP (MoF plan); the Sejm completed the 2026 budget on 9 Jan (deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn); presidential vetoes cost ~PLN 1.8bn in 2026 (Neneman, 9 Jan); budget cash PLN 133.8bn at end-Dec (MoF, 9 Jan).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions: PLN 13.7bn sold on 9 Jan, next 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% (last on 3 Dec); CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec; final on 15 Jan, core estimated ~2.8% by Erste), the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan). GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 9 Jan: the MoF auction sold PLN 12.0bn (demand 22.3bn) plus 1.69bn in the additional sale, DS1035 at 5.121%; US payrolls +50k (about 70k expected), unemployment 4.4%, January Fed cut odds fell to ~3%; no Supreme Court tariff ruling. Prefinancing of 2026 needs at end-2025 was ~21% (final), budget cash PLN 133.8bn. The Sejm finished the 2026 budget. Over the weekend: a Russian missile strike near Lviv; EU states approved the Mercosur deal; the French Assembly committee rejected the 2026 budget. Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10 (reached by 7 Jan, PKO); Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading follows MoF's Q1 issuance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); no switch auction in January; 36-week T-bill auction on 16 Jan (PLN 2-4bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn). MoF priced EUR 3.25bn on 8 Jan (EUR 2bn Jan-2031 at 2.964%, MS+43; EUR 1.25bn Jun-2036 at 3.739%, MS+83). 9 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn sold vs 22.3bn demand (cover 1.86) plus 1.69bn additional sale (DS1035 1.17bn); stop yields OK0128 3.678%, PS0130 4.258%, PS0131 4.504%, DS1033 4.851%, DS1035 5.121%; new NZ0331 PLN 1.26bn at 95.20. Prefinancing at end-2025 was ~21% (final). BGK FPC auction today (12 Jan: FPC0229, FPC0231, FPC0332, FPC0235; min PLN 1.0bn).
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. The 9 Jan auction cleared PLN 13.7bn with 1.86x cover, so supply is being absorbed; 22 and 28 Jan remain (PLN 15-25bn). For the front end the 13-14 Jan MPC is the event: a hold is the consensus, but Dąbrowski's 50% (8 Jan) means a cut is partly priced; the December final CPI (15 Jan) and the March projection drive the timing.

core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~55bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00%, the Fed and BoE are easing gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 60bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 233bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 9 Jan close; ~10bp less here on DS1035 vs the Bundesbank fitted 10Y). US payrolls +50k (9 Jan) pushed the next Fed cut out to June; OAT-Bund 66bp, BTP-Bund 64bp (9 Jan closes).
